To facilitate the computation of PUE, the model incorporates the following assumptions.  Steady-state operation  Neglecting both kinetic and potential energy changes, as well as heat losses  Fully developed flow and thermal conditions  Lumped parameter approach to the radiator  Negligible conduction resistance in radiator heat transfer  Ideal overall surface efficiency of the radiator fins Figure 18 shows the components of the model. The radiator is the primary focus of analysis for predicting PUE using the semiempirical lumped model. The fan and coolant pump are evaluated in relation to their respective flow rates and power consumptions, which are correlated with the radiator through energy balance, the effectiveness-NTU method, and empirical data. The heater serves as the sole heat source (simulating IT loads), and the condenser is assumed to transfer all the heat generated by the heater to the radiator via the coolant, based on the energy balance analysis.
